clue.text: This chap is in love with Rosalind, madly

definitions.text: This chap is in love with Rosalind, madly

parts.words: This chap is in love with Rosalind, madly
parts.note: points to the young hero of Shakespeare's As You Like It, who pins love poems to trees for Rosalind; Ariosto's mad knight of the same name lurks behind 'madly'

explanation.surface: A man is head over heels for a woman called Rosalind.
explanation.definitionFit: The lovesick hero of As You Like It, wooer of Rosalind in the Forest of Arden, bears this name.

clue.text: Informed about article covering social event

indicators.note: covering puts the article above the event in this down entry

parts.note: on means about or concerning
the is the definite article
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece reports a society party.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert and well briefed is an idiom for knowing what is going on.

clue.text: What could make letter rubbish?

parts.note: a printer's misprint could change one vowel so a written message becomes discarded refuse

explanation.surface: Someone asks what might spoil a piece of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: In printing, a typo is called by this name; one swapping E for I makes LETTER into LITTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A printer's error of a single character is a typo in old trade jargon.

clue.text: Former PM meets celebrity, a guiding light

parts.note: Lord North was British prime minister 1770-82
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: An ex-premier meets a famous figure who inspires him.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, used by navigators to find direction, literally guides travellers.

clue.text: Russian girl in river there, topless

indicators.note: topless says the first letter of the river is removed

parts.note: the Volga is the great river of Russia

explanation.surface: A Russian woman sunbathes topless by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' points back to Russia: VOLGA less its top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Russian female first name.

clue.text: Look for expert with a remedy for all

parts.note: to pan for gold is to search for it, so look for gives PAN
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Someone goes in search of a specialist who has a cure-all.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure-all, a single medicine for every ailment, is the literal sense of the Greek-derived word.

clue.text: Small flame gets one and all in a quandary

indicators.note: in places the pieces within the word for quandary

parts.note: a plight is a predicament or quandary
one is I, the Roman numeral
the lot means all of it

explanation.surface: Someone finds everyone caught up in a dilemma.
explanation.definitionFit: The small permanent burner that ignites a gas boiler.

clue.text: Racket revealed by informer, one inside

indicators.note: inside says the numeral goes within the word for informer

parts.note: a nose is slang for a police informer
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A gang's fraud is exposed by an insider who grassed.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud din is a racket.

clue.text: Caught girl swallowing last of hooch in cup

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: last of asks for the final letter of hooch

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is caught downing the dregs of illicit liquor from a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet, especially the communion cup, is a cup.

clue.text: Comply with order given to reluctant players?

definitions.meaning: to follow advice or instructions is to obey them
a director might urge hesitant actors to perform

explanation.surface: A theatre director barks commands at unwilling cast members.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow instructions is to proceed upon them; literally, a command to perform.

clue.text: Master tactician's first in defeat to be taken aback

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the whole built-up word is read in reverse
says one piece goes inside the other word

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of tactician's

explanation.surface: A master strategist is shocked to be beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes into ROUT to make ROTUT, which 'taken aback' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A private teacher or schoolmaster is a coach for pupils.

clue.text: Flirt with ladies' man around teatime?

indicators.note: around says the first word wraps itself about the second

parts.note: a gallant is a man attentive to women
tea is traditionally at four o'clock, IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A woman flirts with a womaniser over afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the stretch: teatime is four o'clock, written IV.
explanation.definitionFit: To gad about seeking pleasure, often amorous, is to roam flirtatiously.

clue.text: Crude burrow at end of gully

parts.note: a fox's burrow is called its earth

indicators.note: end of asks for the last letter of gully

explanation.surface: A rough hole is dug at the bottom of a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse, unrefined humour is called crude or down-to-earth.

clue.text: From Attica, then, I anciently derived

definitions.text: From Attica, then, I anciently derived

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone claims ancient descent from the region of Greece around Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the end of Attica and the words then, I and the start of anciently.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Athens, the chief city of Attica, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Like Don Juan, smart enough to get aphrodisiac

parts.note: Don Juan, the legendary seducer, came from Spain
fly is slang for sharp or smart

explanation.surface: A seducer is clever enough to obtain a love potion.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantharides, a beetle preparation, was reputed to arouse desire.

clue.text: Apportion a return of tax

indicators.note: return means the word for tax is read backwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax

explanation.surface: A taxpayer is told to share out a tax rebate.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or share out portions.

clue.text: Minister with unfortunate ties surrounded by crowd

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the jumbled letters inside the word for crowd

parts.note: a press is a crowd or throng

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests the letters of ties have come out badly arranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman in an ugly tie is mobbed.
explanation.walkthrough: IESTE, from 'unfortunate' ties, goes inside PRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman serving as a religious officiant ministers to worshippers.

clue.text: If one's brought in new design, it's imported

indicators.note: brought in says the pieces are placed inside the rearranged word
new says the letters of design are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is is, a link

explanation.surface: Fresh design, once included, signals something brought from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' design gives SIGNED, and IF plus I go inside it. Import here means significance, not goods from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To import is an old verb for to mean or betoken, so this is meant.

clue.text: Random inspection in position, leading to arrest

indicators.note: leading to puts the place-word ahead of the arrest-word in the down entry

parts.note: a spot is a position
to check is to halt or arrest

explanation.surface: Police take up position and spot-search before making an arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: An unannounced test on a sample is a random inspection.

clue.text: It may prove difficult to get out of bra, thinly fashioned

definitions.text: It may prove difficult to get out of

indicators.note: fashioned means the letters of bra, thinly are shaped into something new

explanation.surface: A flimsy bra might be hard to wriggle out of.
explanation.definitionFit: A maze is a structure designed so that escape is hard.

clue.text: Fabric's a dollar, then pound

parts.note: a buck is slang for a dollar
to ram is to pound or batter

explanation.surface: Cloth costs a dollar, then a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff cotton or linen cloth used in bookbinding and hats.

clue.text: Gadget army medic used on soldiers

indicators.note: used on says the medic is placed after the soldiers in this across entry

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A medical officer tries a device out on the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A contraption or gizmo is a gadget.

clue.text: Romans wandering round centre of new Italian resort

indicators.note: round says the jumbled letters go about the middle letter
wandering suggests the letters of Romans have strayed
centre of asks for the middle letter of new

explanation.surface: Romans stroll about the middle of a new Riviera town.
explanation.walkthrough: SANRMO from 'wandering' Romans goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: A town on the Ligurian coast known for its casino and song festival.

clue.text: Feeble fellow, rash, losing head

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter of the word for rash is dropped

parts.note: reckless is another word for rash

explanation.surface: A weak man acts rashly and loses his composure.
explanation.walkthrough: RECKLESS with its head, R, lost leaves ECKLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ineffective and spineless is weak or feeble.

clue.text: As this description of Capone might well have been

definitions.text: As this description of Capone might well have been

parts.words: As this description of Capone might well have been
parts.note: the gangster Al Capone, if stout, could be called by a two-part nickname; the phrase also means deadly, as he was

explanation.surface: A remark on the gangster Al Capone's likely notoriety.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly, as his rivals found, and read as a stout Al.

clue.text: Let down junior

definitions.meaning: of lesser rank, as in a subordinate chamber

explanation.surface: A youngster disappoints.
explanation.definitionFit: To descend or lower something; also, the subordinate rank or school.

clue.text: A movable feast?

parts.note: a church term for a festival of no fixed date, read literally as a meal that can be carried about

explanation.surface: A churchgoer asks about Easter's shifting date.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor meal carried in a hamper is a feast that travels.

clue.text: Such an irritation for Doolittle to get married

indicators.note: Eliza Doolittle of Pygmalion drops her aitches, so the initial letter goes

parts.note: to get hitched is to marry

explanation.surface: Eliza Doolittle finds marriage a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza Doolittle, the Cockney flower girl of Shaw's Pygmalion, drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge to scratch is a minor irritation.

clue.text: Go mad and disconcert a worthy

parts.note: to throw someone is to disconcert them
fit means worthy or suitable

explanation.surface: Someone loses their head and unsettles a dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's temper violently is to go berserk, idiomatically.

clue.text: Girl showing wrath, one having spurned love

parts.note: ire means wrath

indicators.note: having spurned says a letter is rejected from the word one

parts.note: love is zero, O, in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A jilted woman is furious at being turned down by her sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Beat game sucker

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat
game animals are hunted prey

explanation.surface: Someone thrashes a gullible victim of a con.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel-like fish that attaches by a sucking mouth is a sucker.

clue.text: They may be caught at sea and obtained beside quay

definitions.text: They may be caught at sea

parts.note: had means got or obtained
a dock is a quay or wharf

explanation.surface: Fishermen land their catch at the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A North Atlantic food fish, netted by trawlers; the plural form is the same as the singular.
